title: Live isolated browser engine (Playwright-core worker)
objective: Give the existing isolated browser host (SG-000074..SG-000079) a real engine: a constrained Playwright-core worker that drives the installed, verified Edge/Chrome in the Deskal-owned profile, so that already-qualified navigation, observation, actuation and transfer policies act on live pages. First journey: open a controlled site, find a dated report, download the exact PDF into the approved workspace folder and independently verify it. This implements roadmap increment F3 of the adopted plan (docs/aladdin/IMPLEMENTATION_ROADMAP.md).

include: Activate the SG-000108 contract only; the engine, dependency, tools and authority changes require separately exact-head qualified implementation PRs.

Admit exactly playwright-core 1.63.0 (dependency facts under `dependency_admission`) as a pinned, lockfile-recorded dependency of a separate private worker process. The worker requires Node.js 22.14+ and refuses to start without --disable-sigusr1, because natively a same-user process can otherwise activate the Node inspector (a 127.0.0.1:9229 listener). Today the release requires a separately installed Node.js (no runtime is shipped). The general Node.js 20+ prerequisite (SG-000042) is unchanged; when the worker refuses to start (older Node or no flag), the host launcher (slice 2b-ii) reports the browser as typed unavailable. This holds until a signed, pinned Node runtime is admitted under SG-000106. No bundled browser download: the worker drives only the engine the host verified.

Worker transport: private anonymous-pipe IPC with the Rust host using a closed, versioned frame vocabulary that extends the SG-000074 protocol generation (an explicit authority delta of the implementation PR, since SG-000074 currently has no capability frames); no TCP/HTTP listener, no remote-debugging port or address, no generic CDP passthrough. Engine launch and attachment follow `decisions` (PROPOSED) (pipe, host-built argv, OS command-line verification).

Every navigation, redirect, frame, popup, worker, subresource and download decision is made by the existing qdral-browser-host navigation policy (SG-000075) before the worker acts; actual traffic is enforced by host-pinned resolution and a no-route proxy for everything else (see `decisions`, PROPOSED), not by URL interception alone; WebRTC is limited to proxied transport; service workers are blocked and WebSocket traffic is explicitly mediated or denied; page content never becomes policy.
Observation uses Playwright accessibility/aria snapshots mapped onto the SG-000076 bounded, redacted, generation-bound node identity model; caller-supplied selectors are never authority.

Actuation (SG-000077) and transfers (SG-000078) reuse their existing typed shapes; downloads are staged, size/type-checked, digest-recorded and committed create-only inside the approved workspace destination; uploads stay limited to SG-000025/SG-000078-recorded sources.
Exposure follows SG-000079: the live tool set changes only through an explicit, reviewed profile update recorded in discovery, documentation, OAuth scope tables and runtime together.

Test fixtures: an owned controlled fixture site with a dated report list and a known PDF, plus redirect, iframe, shadow-DOM, stale-reference, oversized and forbidden-destination fixtures, served only to the test harness; an independent artifact checker verifies destination bytes, SHA-256 and absence of out-of-scope writes.

TesterArmy E2E (tester-army/e2e) for browser-facing journeys where its engines support the case, ending in deterministic assertions; native Windows UI Automation tests for anything shown in the WPF app.
exclude: Arbitrary JavaScript evaluation, page.evaluate with model- or caller-supplied code, browser_run_code-style tools, generic CDP or DevTools access.
Attaching to, reading cookies from, or exporting state of the user's personal signed-in browser profile (SG-000100 territory).
Bundled browser binaries, runtime npx/@latest installs, or downloads at startup.
Network egress outside the SG-000075 policy, private/loopback/metadata destinations (except the test-only fixture origin, which is never reachable from production configuration), and proxy behavior.
Remote browser control, relay mapping, and Aladdin AI integration (later increments).

authority_delta.activation: None. This packet authorizes implementing and proving SG-000108; it adds no executable, dependency, tool, listener or authority.
authority_delta.browser: Proposed only: after qualification, live navigation, bounded observation, typed actuation and staged create-only downloads in the isolated Deskal browser profile on the verified installed engine, exactly within the already-closed SG-000075..SG-000079 policies.
authority_delta.network: Proposed only: browser traffic limited to SG-000075-admitted public HTTPS destinations; no new listener; the worker reaches the engine only through a host-owned pipe. The controlled fixture origin used by tests is reachable only through a test-only build feature or test-only resolver that cannot be enabled by runtime configuration, and release qualification asserts it is absent.
authority_delta.filesystem: Proposed only: create-only commits of staged downloads inside the approved workspace destination; no other file writes besides the isolated profile directory already owned by the host.
authority_delta.process: Proposed only: one additional supervised worker process owned by the host, placed with the engine in the host's kill-on-close Job Object and terminated with the host; no other process authority.
authority_delta.approval: Unchanged rules: consequential actions and downloads require the existing local approval broker (repaired by #286) with exact digest binding; nothing in the browser mints or reuses approvals.
authority_delta.privileged: None. SG-000096 Full User shell remains unarmed and independent; no elevation, remote full control or personal-profile access.
authority_delta.secrets: No credentials, cookies or session material leave the profile; password and secret fields stay redacted in observations, logs and evidence.
authority_delta.ui_input: None. No desktop input, UI Automation or focus change; the engine stays headless in the isolated profile.

dependency_admission.license: Apache-2.0 (NOTICE retained in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES and the SBOM)
dependency_admission.purpose: Engine protocol, accessibility snapshots, locators, frames, downloads and waits behind the host policies.
dependency_admission.maintenance_signal: Microsoft-maintained, monthly releases (1.62.0 2026-07-24, 1.63.0 2026-09-04, 1.64.0 2026-10-07). 1.63.0 is chosen because 1.64.0 had been public for three days; updates follow the dependency discipline with re-qualification.
dependency_admission.network_behavior: The library performs no network access on import. Its `install`/browser-download commands and any postinstall download are never run: no browser binaries are fetched, npm is run with scripts ignored, and the CLI entry point is not exposed.
dependency_admission.privilege_implications: The worker runs with the user token inside the host Job Object. Code-injection and path-redirection environment variables (NODE_OPTIONS, NODE_PATH, PLAYWRIGHT_*, DEBUG and similar) are stripped from the worker environment; only an explicit allowlist is passed.
dependency_admission.alternatives_considered: A Rust CDP client (deferred in docs/aladdin/ARCHITECTURE.md until measurements justify it); the whole @playwright/mcp package (rejected as a second edge in docs/aladdin/SOURCE_REUSE_MATRIX.md); playwright-core 1.64.0 (too recent).

open_questions: Engine compatibility: playwright-core 1.63.0 against the installed Edge/Chrome versions verified by the host; the supported version window and refusal of unsupported engines.
TesterArmy E2E: exact version, engines and network behavior; it must run only against the controlled fixture origin and must not require a paid or external service.

decisions.question: Engine launch and attachment
decisions.decision: Option (a): the worker launches the host-verified engine with playwright-core launchPersistentContext over --remote-debugging-pipe and ignoreDefaultArgs: true, using exactly the argv, profile and scrubbed environment built by the host. After launch the host compares the OS-reported command line with that argv and refuses any second browser-process engine in its Job Object; this detects drift and does not contain a compromised worker (a recorded residual risk). SG-000074's ALLOWED_FLAGS gains exactly --remote-debugging-pipe, --host-resolver-rules (host-built), --proxy-server=http://0.0.0.0:9, --proxy-bypass-list (host-built), --webrtc-ip-handling-policy=disable_non_proxied_udp and --disable-quic, each accepted only with its host-built or fixed value; FORBIDDEN_FLAGS is unchanged.

decisions.question: Actual-traffic enforcement of SG-000075
decisions.decision: Three fail-closed layers: host-pinned, port-pinned resolution (MAP <name> <select_public_address pin>:443 for each admitted name, then MAP * ~NOTFOUND); no route for IP literals or unmapped names (--proxy-server=http://0.0.0.0:9 with an exact --proxy-bypass-list of admitted names plus <-loopback>; zero accepts by hostile listeners on port 9); and the SG-000075 policy route, with service workers blocked and WebSocket denied. WebRTC UDP, which otherwise bypasses the first two layers, is refused with --webrtc-ip-handling-policy=disable_non_proxied_udp, and QUIC with --disable-quic. The host refuses to launch when any mandatory Edge, Chrome or Chromium policy (HKLM or HKCU) is present, and release qualification re-runs the layer probes on the installed engine.

decisions.question: WebMCP and web extraction scope
decisions.decision: WebMCP is added to SG-000108 as later slices on the isolated worker: read-only discovery (slice 4), then approval-gated execution (slice 5). Native web extraction follows: scrape and Markdown (slice 6), then map and crawl (slice 7). These are Aladdin's own pipeline on the isolated engine; Firecrawl modules may be adapted into it under the founder's source permission of 2026-10-12 (docs/aladdin/SOURCE_PERMISSIONS.md). Page-advertised tools grant nothing; the Rust host validates, approves and bounds every call. Every slice is separately qualified, and this decision grants no authority.

decisions.question: TesterArmy E2E (open question): exact version, engines and network behavior
decisions.decision: e2e 0.20.0 with @e2e-dev/web 0.14.0 (playwright-core 1.63.0, already admitted), installed with --ignore-scripts from a pinned lockfile in a test-only folder. No model and no telemetry (E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1); no browser download. The suite's Edge is launched with the exact production argv and engine environment for the fixture.test destination, accepted by the worker's own launchRefusal, except that the pipe is replaced by loopback DevTools for TesterArmy's CDP attachment. Enforcement is checked outside the browser: LAN listeners (positive control; a negative-control Edge confined to the listener as its proxy) must receive nothing from an IP-literal bypass, and the OS connection tables of the browser's process tree must show no TCP connection or listener beyond loopback and no mDNS socket, with ICE sockets required as proof the WebRTC probe ran. The tables cannot show where a UDP socket sends: UDP egress is observed only at the listener's address. Mutations prove each check. It is an independent black-box check of the first journey and does not test the production worker, whose confinement and policies stay proven by the native suite. OS-enforced containment (WFP or AppContainer) would need system configuration and is not made.

decisions.question: Engine compatibility (open question): the supported version window and refusal of unsupported engines
decisions.decision: The live worker runs only on engine kinds and majors listed in QUALIFIED_WORKER_ENGINES (discovery.rs): Edge 155 (evidence host, native suite with the leak control required) and Chrome 154 (CI windows-latest, the same full native suite). validate_launch refuses any other major or an unparseable version with the typed Unavailable(UnsupportedEngine) before anything is spawned; discovery's kind, path and Authenticode checks are unchanged. A new major is added only by a PR whose own native-suite run on that engine passes; until then the worker is refused on it.

invariants: The Rust host remains the policy authority: the worker never decides navigation, download or exposure on its own and refuses any frame outside the closed vocabulary.
No code path evaluates caller-, model- or page-supplied script; Playwright APIs are called only with host-constructed typed arguments.
Every observation and action is bound to exact page, document and node generations; stale or foreign identities fail closed and require re-observation.
Downloads are never opened, executed or extracted; commit is create-only and reconciled after uncertainty instead of retried blindly.
The worker, the engine and their descendants are supervised and terminated with the host (Job Object kill-on-close); a crashed worker yields a typed failure, never a fabricated success.
The production configuration cannot reach the test fixture origin; fixture allowances are test-only and asserted absent in release qualification.
SG-000096 and SG-000108 touch disjoint authority (process/shell vs isolated browser) and may proceed in parallel by founder decision of 2026-10-10; neither grain may widen the other's surface.

acceptance.claim: Activation is authority-neutral on base 37a1a0f9f3e530d6fdef998301f975752f8c991a (main after #282), records the founder decision to run in parallel with SG-000096 (evidence: issue #290), and imports no code.

playwright-core 1.63.0 is admitted with exact integrity, license notice, SBOM entry and provenance as in `dependency_admission`; the lockfile delta matches exactly; no other package is added; no browser download or install script runs; the worker environment allowlist is tested.

Host-to-worker IPC is closed and versioned; unknown frames, script evaluation, generic CDP and caller selectors are rejected by construction and by negative tests; the engine runs with exactly the host-built argv of the engine-attachment decision, verified against the OS-reported command line, and the SG-000074 argv change is recorded as an explicit authority delta.

Live navigation on the verified installed engine obeys every SG-000075 rule against real traffic (redirect widening, downgrade, rebinding, private/loopback/metadata, frames/popups/workers, service workers blocked, WebSocket denied, WebRTC UDP refused, QUIC and WebTransport refused, non-443 ports and managed-policy overrides refused), proven with fixtures; the resolver-pinning and no-route layers are each proven with the policy route disabled by a test-only hook.
Bounded observation over real pages including shadow DOM and iframes maps onto SG-000076 identities with redaction, ceilings and generation checks.

First journey passes end to end on native Windows: open the controlled site, select the latest report by declared date, obtain approval, download the exact PDF create-only into the approved folder, and the independent checker verifies bytes and SHA-256; forbidden redirects, oversized files, path traversal and existing-file conflicts are refused; cancellation, timeout and worker crash produce typed outcomes and no partial commit.
Exposure, discovery, documentation and OAuth scope tables agree mechanically for any tool added; remote mapping stays disabled.

Exact-head CI, genuine Jev, Alibaba OpenCodeReview delegation with manual exclusions, PStack review and close-out, native Windows evidence and TesterArmy E2E evidence (fixture origin only, no paid or external service) are recorded; normal merge and post-merge CI.

Profile isolation: only the Deskal-owned profile adopted by the host is used, its fingerprint marker is re-checked before each launch, personal-profile and browser-state environment variables are scrubbed, and no cookies, credentials or history leave it.

Engine compatibility: the supported Edge/Chrome version window for playwright-core 1.63.0 is enforced together with the host signature verification; unsupported engines are refused with a typed error.

Supervision: worker and engine are in the host kill-on-close Job Object; native tests kill the host, the worker and the engine in turn and show no process survives and no partial download is committed; the measured process count stays within the job's active-process limit and the debugging-pipe handles are not inherited by engine child processes.
Size: the worker package and dependency add a measured amount to the installed release, and the full installed application stays below the 400 MB target.
Any live tool is a subset of the twelve SG-000079 browser_structured shapes; the exposure profile, discovery, documentation and OAuth scope tables change together.
